why: Fix the common distinct count d (only 1..26 possible) and count cut patterns with a prefix DP: ways_d[i] sums ways_d[j] over the start positions j where value[j:i] has exactly d distinct letters. Those j form one contiguous range, so a prefix sum answers each step in O(1).
hints: The number of distinct letters in a part is between 1 and 26. Try solving the problem for one fixed d and add the answers.

For a fixed end i, the distinct count of value[j:i] only grows as j moves left, and it jumps exactly at the last occurrences of each letter before i. So the j's with exactly d distinct letters lie between the d-th and (d+1)-th most recent last-occurrence.
Keep the last-occurrence positions sorted (at most 26), one ways array plus prefix sum per d, and sum ways_d[n] over d. O(26 * n) time, take everything mod 1e9+7.
pitfalls: The whole string as one part is always valid; make sure ways_d[0] = 1 for every d so it is counted.
Do not count a partition once per d; each partition has exactly one d, so summing over d is correct, but only if each d's DP is kept separate.
An O(n^2) scan of all cuts times out at n = 100000.
Apply the modulo when subtracting prefix sums (keep results non-negative).
